concept.name: Variable index dynamic average
concept.definition: Tushar Chande's Variable Index Dynamic Average: an exponential-style moving average whose smoothing constant is scaled each bar by a volatility index — the absolute Chande Momentum Oscillator — so it reacts faster in decisive, volatile markets and slower in quiet ones.
concept.intuition: An adaptive average that automatically speeds up when the market is moving decisively and slows down when it is drifting.
concept.mechanics: VIDYA_t = VIDYA_{t-1} + alpha * |CMO_t|/100 * (P_t - VIDYA_{t-1}), with alpha = 2/(n+1). When |CMO| nears 100 (one-way market) VIDYA behaves like a fast EMA; when CMO nears 0 it barely moves.
concept.formula: VIDYA_t = VIDYA_{t-1} + alpha * (|CMO_t|/100) * (P_t - VIDYA_{t-1}); alpha = 2/(n+1); CMO = 100*(Su - Sd)/(Su + Sd) with Su, Sd the sums of up and down close-to-close changes over the look-back.
concept.failure_modes: In choppy markets CMO hovers near zero and VIDYA effectively freezes, missing genuine moves; results are sensitive to the CMO look-back choice.
concept.misconceptions: VIDYA is not the same as KAMA: KAMA adapts via an efficiency ratio (net change over path length), while VIDYA adapts via a momentum-volatility index.
concept.example: If alpha = 0.2 and the CMO reads +60, the effective smoothing constant is 0.12; at CMO = +10 it falls to 0.02.
